Laptop setup

All the code in this course runs on your own laptop in JupyterLab, and none of it needs an API key or a paid account. Setup takes about 20 minutes, most of which is spent downloading.

Please finish before Thursday 1 October

Campus network slows down when 19 people install libraries at the same moment, so please set up at home or in the hostel. If you get stuck, email the error message and a screenshot before Wednesday evening.

1. Install git and uv

git downloads the course folder and, each week, the new notebooks. uv installs Python and the course libraries. It installs the right Python version for you and downloads libraries much faster than pip, so you do not need to install Python separately. An existing Python or Anaconda installation will not get in the way.

On a Mac, open Terminal and run:

git --version
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

If the first line says git is missing, macOS offers to install the command line developer tools. Accept, wait for it to finish, then run the second line.

On Windows, install git from git-scm.com (the default options are fine). Then open PowerShell and run:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

Then close the terminal window and open a new one, and check that both worked:

git --version
uv --version
The uv install command is blocked, or you would rather not paste it

If you already have Python, pip install uv works too. On a Mac with Homebrew, brew install uv also works.

2. Get the course folder

In your terminal, go to wherever you keep coursework and run:

git clone https://github.com/shripada/ads6703-nlp.git ADS6703

This creates a folder called ADS6703 holding the notebooks, the datasets and the list of libraries. It looks like this, and grows by one folder each week:

ADS6703/
├── requirements.txt       ← the list of libraries (step 3)
├── W00-setup-check.ipynb  ← checks your setup (step 4)
├── data/                  ← the course datasets
├── w01/                   ← Workshop 1 notebooks
├── w02/
└── …

Every notebook loads its data from ../data/, so don't move or rename anything.

Without git: download a ZIP instead

Open the course repo, click the green Code button, then Download ZIP. Unzip it where you keep coursework and rename the folder from ads6703-nlp-main to ADS6703. Each week, download the new notebooks from the workshop page into ADS6703/wNN/, because git pull (step 5) won't work for you.

3. Create your environment and install the libraries

Go into the course folder and run these two commands:

cd ADS6703
uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install -r requirements.txt

The first command downloads Python 3.12 if you don't have it and creates a .venv folder inside ADS6703. The second installs the libraries into it. You never need to "activate" anything, because the uv run command in step 4 finds .venv automatically.

If your prompt starts with a name in brackets, such as (base)

Another Python environment is active (usually Anaconda's), and uv would install into it instead of .venv. Run conda deactivate (or deactivate for other environments) until the brackets disappear, then run the commands above. Do the same before uv run jupyter lab each week.

This installs JupyterLab, pandas, scikit-learn, NLTK, gensim, PyTorch (CPU only) and Hugging Face transformers, about 1 GB in total. One install covers all 12 workshops.

On an Intel Mac (Apple menu → About This Mac shows an Intel processor rather than Apple M1, M2, …), the install stops with a torch error and installs nothing. Follow Torch install fails on an Intel Mac below instead.

4. Check that everything works

From inside your ADS6703 folder, start JupyterLab:

uv run jupyter lab

Open W00-setup-check.ipynb and choose Run → Run All Cells. If every line ends in ✅, you are ready. If any line shows ❌, it tells you what to fix.

5. Every week

Before each class, open a terminal and run:

cd ADS6703
git pull
uv run jupyter lab

git pull brings in that week's notebooks and, after class, the solutions to the previous week's. Work in the notebooks where they are. Published files never change afterwards, so pulling will not clash with your work.

The course data

The datasets are already in ADS6703/data/ if you cloned the repo. If you need them separately, save these files into ADS6703/data/. Do not unzip the .gz files in that folder, because pandas reads them directly. To browse them in Excel, work on a copy (below).

File What it is Size
reviews.csv.gz 30,000 Amazon reviews of appliances and parts. The running case. 3.8 MB
products.csv.gz Metadata (title, price, features, description) for the 946 products that were reviewed. 0.6 MB
support_inbox.csv 300 synthetic customer-support messages, used in the Workshop 1 challenge. 80 KB

Looking at the data in Excel

Scroll through the data yourself before any code touches it. Excel works well for this, but it needs two extra steps. Work on copies, so the files in ADS6703/data/ stay exactly as they are.

  1. Copy the file from ADS6703/data/ to your Desktop.
  2. Unzip it. This applies only to the .gz files; support_inbox.csv is ready as it is.
    • Mac: double-click reviews.csv.gz in Finder. reviews.csv appears next to it.
    • Windows: install 7-Zip (free), then right-click the file → 7-Zip → Extract Here.
  3. Import it into Excel. Don't double-click the .csv: Excel would then garble characters such as ₹, ★ and curly quotes. Instead, open a blank workbook and:
    • Windows: Data → From Text/CSV → choose the file → set File Origin to 65001: Unicode (UTF-8) → Load.
    • Mac: File → Import → CSV file → choose the file → in the wizard, set File origin to Unicode (UTF-8) and keep Delimited → tick Comma → Finish.
  4. To read long reviews, select the text column, click Wrap Text, and widen the column. Data → Filter adds filter buttons to the headers, for example to show only 1★ reviews.

You don't need to save anything. If you do, save it outside ADS6703/data/.

Before Unit 3 (not needed yet)

From Workshop 9 onwards we use small open transformer models (DistilBERT, GPT-2, T5-small), which together come to about 1.5 GB. You will get a one-cell download notebook to run at home the week before. The models run offline, on your laptop's CPU, with no API key.

Troubleshooting

git or uv "not found" or "not recognized"

The terminal you are using was opened before the tool was installed. Close it, open a new one, and try again. On Windows, if git is still not found, reinstall it from git-scm.com with the default options.

git pull says "not a git repository"

You are not inside the ADS6703 folder (run cd ADS6703 first), or you downloaded the ZIP instead of cloning. With the ZIP, download each week's notebooks from the workshop page.

git pull says "your local changes would be overwritten"

This shouldn't happen, because published files never change. Don't delete anything: email me the full message and I'll tell you what to do.

jupyter "not found", or a notebook says a library is missing

Start Jupyter with uv run jupyter lab, not plain jupyter lab, and run it from inside your ADS6703 folder so that uv finds .venv. If you use Anaconda, run conda deactivate first so that conda's Jupyter doesn't get picked up.

The notebook says it can't find ../data/reviews.csv.gz

The notebook must be inside a workshop folder such as ADS6703/w01/, and the data must be in ADS6703/data/. If you downloaded files by hand, check that the names have not been changed; for example, some browsers rename downloads to reviews.csv (1).gz.

Torch install fails on an Intel Mac

PyTorch no longer supports Intel Macs, so the whole install stops. You can skip this problem until Unit 3. Remove the torch, transformers and sentencepiece lines from requirements.txt, run uv pip install -r requirements.txt again, and talk to me before Workshop 9. (Editing requirements.txt is the one exception to "don't change published files". If git pull later complains about it, run git checkout requirements.txt and pull again.)

I'd rather keep using Anaconda

That's fine if your Anaconda already works. Run conda create -n nlp python=3.12 -y, then conda activate nlp, then pip install -r requirements.txt from your ADS6703 folder. Activate nlp and run plain jupyter lab each time. The rest of this page is the same.
